title: Lentivirus-mediated gene delivery to study neurogenesis in adult rodents
author: Xu, Tang
materials:

Note: The components and storage methods are described in the Materials and Equipment section.

steps.title: Extract plasmids for lentivirus
steps.instruction: Isolate the target lentiviral plasmid (CAG‑PTN‑2A‑GFP, >150 µg) and the three helper plasmids (VSVG >40 µg, pMDLg >100 µg, pRSV‑Rev >55 µg).

steps.title: Prepare transfection reagents
steps.instruction: Gather DMEM (4 °C storage), FBS (‑20 °C), penicillin‑streptomycin (‑20 °C), Opti‑MEM I (4 °C), PEI (1 mg/mL, 4 °C, 12 mo), and DPBS (25 °C).

steps.title: Seed HEK293T cells for packaging
steps.instruction: Plate HEK293T cells into five 150 mm dishes, each with 13 mL culture medium, and incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ until 80 % confluent (one dish must reach 95‑100 % before splitting).

steps.title: Sterilize surgical instruments and equipment
steps.instruction: Autoclave scissors, blunt‑end forceps, needle holder, scalpel, cotton swabs, absorbable sutures, and electric razor; sterilize the surgical field by UV irradiation.

steps.title: Prepare surgical reagents and mice
steps.instruction: Set out 75 % ethanol, isoflurane, ketoprofen, erythromycin eye ointment, and the lentivirus stock; select 12‑month‑old C57BL/6 male or female mice and house them on a 12‑h light/dark cycle with ad libitum food and water.

steps.title: Prepare EdU/BrdU stock solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 10 mg EdU or BrdU in 1 mL DPBS (10 mg/mL) by vortexing; heat to 42 °C if needed; store powder at –20 °C protected from light and prepare fresh solution for each use.

steps.title: Prepare tissue fixation and staining solutions
steps.instruction: Make 0.2 M phosphate buffer (store 25 °C, ≤1 mo), 4 % PFA (store 4 °C, ≤2 wks, protected from light), cryoprotectant (store 4 °C, ≤1 mo), Click Additive Solution per manufacturer (store –20 °C after dispensing), and PVA‑DABCO (store –20 °C ≤6 mo, 4 °C ≤1 wk).

steps.title: Assemble stereotaxic setup and anesthetize mouse
steps.instruction: Mount the stereotaxic frame, dental drill, and anesthesia machine; induce anesthesia with 5 % isoflurane in air, then maintain at 2 % (alternatives: sodium pentobarbital 50 mg/kg i.p. or avertin 400 mg/kg i.p.). Inject ketoprofen 3–5 mg/kg i.p. for analgesia (alternative: carprofen 5–10 mg/kg s.c.). Place mouse on a heating pad, apply erythromycin eye ointment, shave the head with an electric razor, and disinfect skin with 75 % ethanol (alternating with iodine if desired).

steps.title: Perform stereotactic lentiviral injection
steps.instruction: Secure the mouse in the stereotaxic frame, adjusting ear bars to avoid loose head or excess pressure; drill two skull holes at coordinates AP 2.0 mm, ML ±1.7 mm, DV –1.9 mm; load a 5 µL Hamilton syringe with a 33‑gauge needle with lentivirus; inject at 0.2 µL/min using the syringe pump; close the incision and keep the mouse on a heating pad until fully recovered.

steps.title: Perfuse, fix, and section brain
steps.instruction: Anesthetize the mouse, perfuse transcardially with 0.01 M PBS followed by 4 % PFA; post‑fix brain in 4 % PFA for 24 h; equilibrate in 30 % sucrose at 4 °C for 2 days; cut 40 µm coronal sections with a sliding microtome; store floating sections in cryoprotectant at 4 °C in 96‑well plates.

substeps.instruction: Wash floating sections 3 × 5 min with 0.01 M PBS at 25 °C, gentle shaking.
Incubate in PBS 0.5 % Triton for 20 min at 25 °C.
Prepare Click Reaction Solution (total 500 µL): 430 µL Click reaction buffer, 20 µL CuSO₄, 1 µL Azide 568, 50 µL Click Additive Solution; mix in order, use within 15 min, protect from light.
Incubate sections with Click Reaction Solution (500 µL per well) at 25 °C for 30 min, protected from light.
Block with buffer containing 300 µL goat serum and 250 µL 10 % Triton X‑100 per 10 mL for 1 h at 25 °C, gentle shaking.
Incubate with primary antibody (Rabbit anti‑GFAP 1:1000 in blocking buffer) at 4 °C for 24 h, gentle shaking.
Incubate with secondary antibody (1:1000 in PBS) at 25 °C for 1–2 h, gentle shaking.
Mount sections with PVA‑DABCO, coverslip, and let dry completely before imaging.
Repeat washing and Triton permeabilization steps from EdU protocol.
Incubate in 2 M HCl at 37 °C for 20 min (pre‑warmed water bath).
Rinse, then incubate in 0.1 M Borate buffer (pH 8.0) at 25 °C for 20 min on a shaker; ensure HCl is fully removed.
Repeat wash and block steps from EdU protocol.
Incubate with primary antibodies (Rat anti‑BrdU 1:1000, Mouse anti‑DCX 1:200, or Rabbit anti‑NeuN 1:500) diluted in blocking buffer at 4 °C for 24 h, gentle shaking.
Proceed with secondary antibody incubation, washing, and mounting as described in the EdU protocol.

description: Stereotactic lentiviral injection is a relatively rapid method to assess up- or down-regulation of different genes in vivo, which is widely applicated in the studies on neurodegenerative and neuropsychiatric disorders.2,3 Pleiotrophin (PTN), is a developmentally regulated and secreted growth factor, which has been identified that adult mouse hippocampal NSCs-derived PTN regulates newborn neuron development.3 To investigate whether autocrine PTN signaling could improve adult hippocampal neurogenesis, we delivered lentivirus expressing PTN into the DG of rodent hippocampus. Among all the experimental steps, placement of a mouse in a stereotactic frame is one of the most critical steps of this surgery. Majority of the issues happen here due to a loose head, or injury due to an excessive pressure. Therefore, it requires training and knowledge in how much the ear bars can be pushed towards the mouse skull. Here, this approach describes how to deliver lentiviruses (LVs) to target brain regions in rodents via stereotactic injection in detail.Note: Within each step of the protocol, if the recommended reagent/equipment is not available, you may try a product with similar functionality.CRITICAL: It is highly recommended that people learn about vernier scales and safe mouse positioning before performing stereotactic injections.
